correctness.rationale: For each alpha the explicitly feasible human/AV split satisfies all 3-path Wardrop/marginal-cost inequalities. The two cost differences are direct identities; K>0 ensures AV strictly use outer paths. The strict positive affine delays satisfy the hypotheses of the source's aggregate-link-flow uniqueness theorem, whose Appendix II argument was read, hence all equilibria have the same shortcut flow. Direct edge-delay expansion proves the welfare polynomial; positivity of K,L gives plateau, strict decline and full-altruistic optimum. The rational family satisfies every strict hypothesis and exhibits an exact gap tending to 1. Exact-rational checker replays identity tests but is not an infinite proof. No stochastic or atomic extension claimed.

value.rationale: The minimally connected standard Braess paradox graph is mathematically natural, not an arbitrary numerical network. Exact classification for every penetration fraction gives a policy-relevant first-effective-adoption threshold and the full attainable performance law, rather than an elementary endpoint calculation. The parameter family proves arbitrarily near-total altruistic adoption can leave an O(1) absolute delay gap unchanged, a substantive warning not implied by merely knowing plateaus exist. The result deliberately makes no claim of general-network applicability.
